title: fix(post): a touch probe section starts no spindle on any mill post
body:
## What changed

A touch probe is never spun (#523). Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain and Mazak posted `S<rpm> M3` (Mazak `MOTON S…`) for every section, a probe's S0 included. Each now gates its spindle start on `sRpm > 0`, the rule `fanuc.cps` has used since #108. Heidenhain also drops the `S` word from its `TOOL CALL` at rpm 0.

- No extra `M5` is needed: every post already ends each section with `M5`, so a probe section never inherits a running spindle.
- A cutter can never lose its spindle through this: `Tool::is_sane` refuses rpm 0 on every tool, so S0 reaches a post only from a probe dump.
- **Reachability:** on main, only Fanuc posts probe moves, and it was already gated. PR #500 (Tormach probe positioning) makes the Tormach path reachable, which is where `S0 M3` showed up in the Hub run. #500 should merge after this.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/probe_spindle.rs`:
- `a_section_with_no_spindle_speed_starts_no_spindle_on_any_mill_post`: an rpm-0 section through all six mill posts posts no `S` word and no `M3`/`M03`/`MOTON`. It fails without the post changes (`haas: a probe section posts ["S0", "M3"]`).
- `a_cutting_section_still_starts_its_spindle_on_every_mill_post`: an 8000 rpm section still posts its `S` word and spindle start on all six.

`scripts/gate.sh quick`, which escalated to batch, ran 782 s. Results:
- geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion: green.
- app: green, 1433 passed and 0 failed across all binaries, conformance and every NC golden byte-exact.
- clippy `-D warnings` on all 8 crates: green.
- ui: the only red is the five known failures that are also red on main: the three headless tests that need a GPU adapter, and `structural::shell_structure_dark/light` (the `v0.0.0` label).

## Not exercised

No Hub run. No posted program on main reaches the changed path except through Fanuc, which is unchanged. Cutting output is byte-identical, since every golden is unchanged.

Changelog: A probing section no longer starts the spindle (S0 M3) on the Haas, Tormach, Siemens, Heidenhain and Mazak posts (#523)

﻿Answers the docs lane of #291 with two pieces, per the plan discussed there.

**`examples/`** - a complete `first-part.camproj` the guide can teach on: our own clean-room flange fixture (model embedded as facets, so the file is self-contained), stock, Face / 2D Pocket / Drill with generated toolpaths, and the posted `first-part.nc`. Built end-to-end through the MCP server; verify is clean; it round-trips through File > Open.

**`docs/images/first-part-*.png`** - four tutorial step pictures that are golden files, not hand-captured screenshots. The docs test in `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs` opens the project through the real open command, steps through `operation_order`, and renders each step with the real viewport pipelines and the real toolpath display (`interact::toolpath_lines`). A normal run compares and fails on drift; `UPDATE_DOCS_IMAGES=1` regenerates - same workflow as the kittest snapshots.

Notes:
- The test lives in the existing `gpu_render` binary on purpose: it shares that binary's GPU lock and adds no new test process (a fifth process racing fallback-device creation across processes is what makes full-suite runs flake).

- `interact::toolpath_lines`: `pub(crate)` -> `pub` so the test draws through the app's own path display.

Test stability: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render` is 10/10 across repeated runs and deterministic through a regen/compare round-trip. The full-suite wgpu flake is pre-existing on `main` (untouched baseline crashed 3 of 4 runs on this machine) and unrelated to this change.

Keeping this draft until the open questions in #291 are answered - images can move to `docs/guide/src/images/` when the mdbook scaffold lands.

title: fix(ui): browser tree rows read on the light panel
body:
## What changed

The browser tree's rows were pale grey on the light panel (#506).

- **Root cause:** egui keeps a dark and a light style and follows the OS appearance. `theme::apply_to` wrote the token table only into the slot that was active at startup. On a Mac in light mode, egui switched to its stock light visuals while the painted tree kept drawing our table's ink on that panel. `apply_to` now writes the table into **both** slots, so the document's theme is the only theme.
- **Row ink:** tree rows no longer use `text_faint`, the disabled tier, which reads about 3:1 on the light strip. A hidden row and the suffix use `text_dim`. A selected row is all `text`, because `text_dim` reads only 3.5:1 on the dark theme's selection fill. The rule lives in `painted::row_inks`.

- New `egui_app::tree_ink_tests` (lib):

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Haas, Mazak and Siemens posts
body:
**Replaces #360** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which touches every `.cps` post). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #173 work itself is the last commit. Review #333 first.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps`: probes.** It adds `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult`:
  - G31 skip; #5061–#5063 trip read; no-contact and out-of-tolerance alarms through `#3000`;
  - incremental G91 back-off;
  - `G10 L2 P` from `#5221+20×slot`, or a `#3006` operator stop.
  - Source: the Haas Mill Operator's Manual (public).
- **`mazak.cps`: probes.** The same macro-B contract in Mazak EIA/ISO words:
  - `IF[..]GOTO` with unique N labels, since `IF..THEN` is not documented on every EIA generation;
  - the operator stop is a comment plus M00.
  - Source: Mazak's EIA/ISO programming manual (Fanuc-compatible).
- **`sinumerik.cps`: probes.**
  - `MEAS=1 G1`; `$AC_MEA[1]` checks for no contact; `$AA_MW[..]` reads the trip into R50–R61.
  - `IF..ENDIF` + `MSG` + `SETAL` + `M0` alarms; incremental G91 back-off.
  - Sets the offset through `$P_UIFR[..,TR]` (FI copied when the frame changes), then re-selects the active G5x.
  - It refuses by name to set G58/G59 (axial offsets on an 840D) or to work from an offset outside G54–G57 / G505–G599.
  - Source: SINUMERIK 840D sl Programming Manual (Fundamentals / Job Planning).
- **`heidenhain.cps`: still refused by name.** The TNC 640 ISO manual this post follows documents no skip move and no trip-position variable; TNC probing lives in the separate touch-probe-cycles manual. The script now carries a comment saying so, and the existing engine refusal is pinned.
- **Spindle at 0 rpm.** Haas, Mazak and Siemens no longer write a spindle-on block at 0 rpm (a touch probe), as fanuc already did. No existing golden contained `S0`.
- `docs/decisions/173-probe-hooks-dialects.md` names every source and judgement call.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_dialects.rs` (7 tests): bore-centre goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/probe_bore_centre.nc` (G55 set from G54), both operator-stop variants, the Sinumerik G59 refusal, and the Heidenhain refusal.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): post suites ok. App suites: everything passes except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`. That test pins `PROJECT_VERSION == 51`, but main is now at 53, so it fails the same way on `upstream/main`; PR #345 fixes it. This commit touches no Rust source.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **No controller or simulator run yet**, so this stays a draft. The posted words follow the public manuals only.
  - Mazak is the weakest-sourced: its `#5061` / `#5221` numbering should be confirmed against a Mazak manual.
  - Sinumerik's MEAS/`$AA_MW` path needs a check on a real 840D or a simulator.
- **The probe is not armed by the post.** Arming is machine-specific and stated by no stream record. An unarmed probe never trips, so it raises the no-contact alarm, which matches fanuc.

title: feat(post): probing hooks for the Tormach PathPilot post (G38.2)
body:
**Replaces #376** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which also edits `tormach.cps`). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #362 work is the last commit (55b7b83).

## What changed
`assets/posts/tormach.cps` gains `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult` in LinuxCNC/PathPilot words, so a Probe op posts on the Tormach mills instead of being refused by name.

**The touch move**
- It is `G38.2`. The control halts with an error when contact never comes, or when the probe is already tripped at the start, so the post writes no no-contact test of its own.
- XY is positioned first, so a probe never starts from an unknown XY.
- `G38.3` plus a `#5070` test was rejected: it hands that safety from the control to our own branch.

**Reading the trip**
- It is read from `#5061`–`#5063`. These are in the coordinate system the G38 ran in, in program units, so they compare directly with the expected values.

**Back-off and tolerance alarm**
- The back-off is incremental (`G91 G1 … G90`).
- A deviation past the tolerance runs `o9nn if [ABS[#19x] GT tol]` / `(MSG, …)` / `M2` / `o9nn endif`, with a unique O-word per test.
- `M2`, not `M0`, so the operator can't resume onto a wrong offset. `(ABORT,…)` is not in the stable LinuxCNC reference.

**Setting the offset**
- `G10 L20 P<n> X[#5420-#190] …`: the current position in the active offset, minus the deviation. It is exact in either unit.
- `G10 L2` from `#5221+20×slot` was rejected: the reference doesn't say which unit the stored offsets use, so a G21 program on an inch-configured control could mix units.
- With no offset to set, it writes `(MSG, CHECK PROBE RESULT …)` then `M0`.

**Preamble**
- A section at 0 rpm (a touch probe) writes no spindle start, no belt note and no coolant.

**Arming**
- Nothing is written. PathPilot's probe input is always live, and the probe type is a Settings-tab choice.

The sources for every word are in `docs/decisions/362-tormach-probe.md`: the LinuxCNC G-code reference, overview and o-code pages, and Tormach's PathPilot post-processor guidelines and G38.x pages. No other CAM system's output was read.

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/probe_tormach.rs` (7 tests). Goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/` on the 770MX (inch): `probe_face`, `probe_edge`, `probe_corner`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_boss_centre`, plus metric `probe_bore_centre_mm`.
- `probe_op::the_tormach_post_probes_the_op_with_g38_2`: the op now posts on Tormach, where it used to be refused.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS): post and app suites all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until done)
These still need a run in PathPilot Hub (770MX), which the contributor will do:
1. Whether preview stops at the first `M2`. In preview, probe moves report the programmed end point, so tolerance tests may read as failed there.
2. That the G91 back-off right after a trip doesn't raise "probe tripped during non-probe move".
3. That `o9nn if`/`endif` is accepted and `(MSG, …)` shows.
4. That `G10 L20 P2` writes G55 correctly, inch and metric.
5. That a trip during the plain G1 descent errors (relevant to #174).
6. That G38.2 errors cleanly with no contact.

Changelog: The Tormach PathPilot post writes the Probe operation (G38.2 touch, tolerance alarm, G10 L20 work offset) instead of refusing it (#362)

Fixes #362

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).

title: fix(app): a typed Slot's caps no longer read as a gouge
body:
## What changed

A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round caps was reported as a Gouge on every plunge and feed, so it never posted (#510). The cause was the region the verifier checks a Slot against, `operation::material::stadium`. It drew each cap as 16 chords **inscribed** in the true arc. A chord sits up to `h(1 - cos 5.625°)` inside the arc, and the slot generator's passes follow the true arc exactly, so the gouge check (`d(centre, boundary) >= r - GOUGE_TOL`) flagged a cutter that only touched the cap.

The caps are now the polygon **circumscribed** about the arc. Every chord is tangent to the arc, and the corners sit at `h / cos(phi/2)`. The chord count is set per slot (`cap_segments`) so a corner stands at most `CAP_SAG_BUDGET = 0.001 mm` outside the arc, with 16 to 2048 chords per cap. The first and last corner of each cap lie on the lines of the straight sides, so the sides stay exact. `GOUGE_TOL` is unchanged.

**Posted G-code: unchanged.** The generator is untouched. Only the gouge verdict changes, plus the drawn region outline, which moves by at most 1 µm.

## Readings (80×60×20 stock, EM-0600-4FL, a=(-15,0), b=(15,0), Top 20, Bottom 10, stepdown 5)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| width 6 (centreline pass) | `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| width 10 (rings at ±2) | `Gouge` on all 18 plunges/feeds; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| cap-centre distance to boundary (r = 3) | 2.9855 (needs ≥ 2.99) | ≥ 3.0 (tangent) |
| path pushed +0.05 mm in X past the cap | (already convicted) | still convicted |

## Top-Z pass

The issue also reports that a Slot makes a feed pass at its Top before stepping down. The other 2D ladders do the same: `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts at Top for pocket, contour, circular, trace, face and the 3D entries. It is an air pass, never a gouge. This PR pins the current behaviour rather than changing one op on its own. The decision file explains why and recommends a separate issue if the first level should be `top - stepdown` for every ladder.

## Tests

New `crates/app/tests/slot_caps.rs`:
- `a_slot_riding_its_round_caps_verifies_clean_and_posts`: widths 6 and 10, each run with stock as the source and with a slotted part model as the source. Each run has no Gouge, no warning that blocks posting, and `post_setup` writes the program.
- `a_slot_driven_past_its_cap_is_still_a_gouge`: the generated path, shifted 0.05 mm past the cap and checked against the op's own `region_of`, is convicted. The unshifted path checks clean.
- `the_stadium_region_hugs_the_true_caps`: at 721 angles on both caps, the true arc is inside the region and a point 2 µm past it is outside.
- `the_slot_ladder_starts_at_the_authored_top`: the cut levels are [20, 15, 10].

Before the fix, the first three fail and the fourth passes.

Gate (debug): camcraft-app lib (101), slot_caps, operations, area_controls, cutting_data, project_roundtrip, golden_cl, verify and blind_floor all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The release `--ignored` lanes. No goldens move, because the generator output is unchanged.
- The UI region-outline drawing (the outline moves by at most 1 µm).
- Hand-run in the GUI or on a real machine.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/510-slot-cap-region.md`.

Changelog: A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round ends is no longer falsely reported as a gouge, so it posts again (#510)

Fixes #510

title: feat(app): recognise pockets and slots and turn them into operations
body:
## What changed

Pocket and slot recognition, headless (app layer and MCP; no GUI changes).

- **`camcraft_app::recognize`** (new module: `mod`, `walls`, `shape`, `op`):
  - `pockets_of(world, model)` reads the model's planar-face topology (`geometry::feature`, the same B-rep `list_features` and the pick tools use).
  - A level, up-facing face is a **floor** when the facets across its outer ring rise from it and lean into it (a concave edge), and those walls face each other across the floor.
  - Walled all round, it is a **closed pocket**. With wall-less spans it is an **open pocket**. A straight channel (at least 2 widths long, both long sides walled, each end wholly walled or wholly open, area within 3% of the shape) is a **slot**, with each end open, round or square.
  - Each result carries:
    - the outer ring (world XY, counter-clockwise), island count and area;
    - floor Z, top Z (highest wall point) and depth;
    - the **tightest inside corner radius** (0 = sharp, `None` where no two walls meet) and the **open spans**;
    - for a slot: centreline ends, **width**, length and end kinds.
  - Shoulders, corner steps, top faces and a plate around a boss are not pockets.
- **`recognize::operation_for`** maps a feature onto `CreateOperation`'s inputs, so creating it is one undoable History step with every field editable:
  - a pocket (or a slot with a square closed end, which a round cap would leave standing) becomes a **2D Pocket** on a pick of the floor face, with `bottom_z` at the selection bottom and `top_z` at the selection bottom + depth;
  - a slot with round or open ends becomes a **Slot** along its centreline: width, fixed heights, source stock, open ends running full width out to the floor's edge.
- **MCP `detect_pockets {model, create?, tool?, name?}`** lists the features, each with the floor's `face:0x…` id (the id `list_features` prints) and the operation kind it would create. With `create` it adds that operation, one undo step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/35-pocket-slot-recognition.md`.

Provenance: the concave-edge depression rule follows Joshi & Chang (CAD 20(2), 1988). The minimum-area rectangle follows Freeman & Shapira (CACM 18(7), 1975). No vendor material was consulted.

## How tested

Quick gate, debug: `pocket_recognition` 10/10, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_setup` 18/18, `cli` 2/2, `feature` 3/3. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Pinning tests, on watertight meshes built in code (`crates/app/tests/pocket_support`):
- `a_rectangular_pocket_is_closed_with_sharp_corners`
- `a_pocket_with_corner_radii_reports_its_tightest_corner` (r 4)
- `a_round_ended_closed_slot_is_a_slot_between_its_cap_centres`
- `a_through_slot_is_open_at_both_ends`
- `an_open_slot_with_a_square_end_machines_as_a_pocket`
- `parts_without_pockets_list_none` (plain block, shoulder, corner step, boss)
- `degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` (unknown model; NaN, infinite and zero-area facets; a torn half mesh)
- `a_recognised_pocket_becomes_an_undoable_pocket_that_cuts_to_its_floor`: generates with no Gouge, reaches the floor, stays inside the ring; undo removes it
- `an_open_slot_machined_as_a_pocket_cuts_its_floor_without_a_gouge`
- `a_recognised_slot_becomes_a_slot_cut_along_its_centreline`: checks the path geometry exactly; undo removes it
- MCP: `detect_pockets_lists_a_rounded_pocket_and_creates_its_pocket` (generate + verify ok; undo/redo), `detect_pockets_creates_a_slot_for_a_through_slot`, `detect_pockets_refuses_bad_arguments_by_name`

## Not exercised / known gaps

- **#510 (filed):** every typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is reported as a gouge today, recognised or not. The likely cause is the stadium region's chorded caps measured against `GOUGE_TOL`. Until #510 lands, a recognised slot's Slot op refuses to post. Its test checks the path geometry, not the verifier's verdict.
- **Not recognised:**
  - through pockets / windows (no floor face);
  - non-level floors and tilted setup frames (the read is world +Z);
  - curved slots, T-slots and undercuts.
  - Each level of a stepped pocket is its own feature.
- An open pocket's open side is not written into the area controls' open boundary. The tool's corner radius stays uncut where a wall meets an open edge.
- **GUI entry point:** #511. Not exercised on real STEP parts or by hand. The release-tier heavy lanes were not run.

Changelog: Pocket and slot recognition - `detect_pockets` (MCP) lists a model's closed/open pockets and slots (depth, corner radius, slot width, open sides) and creates the Pocket or Slot that machines one, one undo step (#35)

Fixes #35

title: fix(sim): judge spindle-C moves at the station pose and fixed steel in the machine frame
body:
Fixes a missed fixture hit under a spindle-C turn (#486). Two causes, both reproduced on main first.

## What was wrong
1. **Fixed steel was judged in the part frame only.** For a C move the live tool never leaves its station (+X), so steel there is hit at every C. The part-frame reading only saw it near C 0; `posed_steel::upright_turn` answers Unjudged for that pose, so the part-frame verdict stood. End to end: a Rotary Contour on the mill-turn C bar with a fixed steady at the station had no hit on the far side of the bar (C≈180), and the post gate was silent too.
2. **Steel riding the part was judged at the wrong pose.** `cl::stamp_c` gave every piece of a split move the move's end axis, while mid-turn the tool points along the diagonal. A chuck jaw on the diagonal at holder radius was silent.

## What changed
- `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary.rs`: `split` stamps each piece with the station pose at its own C (the move's axis turned by the turn left in the move). The last piece keeps the move's axis bit for bit. The post writes only C for C moves, so the stream and the `c_axis_helix.nc` golden are unchanged.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/c_steel.rs`:
  - `station_poses` reads each C move's pose from its C, so toolpaths cached before this fix are judged right at the gate without regenerating.
  - `fixed_hits` judges fixed steel in the machine frame along the station ray.
  - The spindle line is recovered from the stamped tips, then from the op's rotary axis, and used only if every tip sits on its ray within 1e-4 mm. With no line, or an arc or non-finite C move, a C move against fixed steel is a hit (fails closed).
- `crates/sim/src/verify/workholding.rs`: both `_held` wrappers judge the station-posed path, then add the machine-frame fixed-steel hits. Add-only: no existing verdict loosens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/486-stamp-c-axis.md`.

## How tested
- sim `c_axis_fixture` (8). Fail on main: `the_machine_meets_fixed_steel_at_the_station_mid_turn` (line given and line unknown), `a_rapid_turn_past_fixed_steel_convicts_as_a_rapid`, `steel_riding_the_part_meets_the_pose_the_turn_passes_through`, `every_stamped_piece_states_the_station_pose_at_its_own_c`. title: fix(sim): a chamfer or deburr owns its declared edge break
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer or a Deburr generated with no warnings, but the post gate then refused it as a gouge. The program sim judged the bevel the op exists to cut against the model's sharp edge. This PR makes the op own its break, the issue's option 1. The bevel comes from the op's **stated** parameters, not from its moves.

- **`cl::EdgeBreak`** (new, `crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`): a record of the break the op was asked to cut. It holds the edge as a polyline at its own height, the bevel depth at the edge, and the slope. `floor_at(x, y)` gives the cone swept along the edge, limited to the stated plan width. It is carried on `cl::Toolpath::breaks` and is empty for every other kind.
- **Generators declare their breaks:**
  - `machining2d::chamfer` declares the picked loops at `top_z`, with depth `width*tan(angle)` and slope `tan(angle)`.
  - `finishing3d::deburr` declares its edge runs, with depth `drop` and slope `cot(half-angle)`.
  - Neither reads the declaration back off the moves.
- **Sim credit** (new, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`, `credit_breaks`): this runs after `deviate`, from `simulate_document`. A gouge column inside a declared break's width, under a model top no higher than the edge, is re-judged against the bevel:
  - Cut down to the bevel (within `DEV_TOL`): clean.
  - Cut below the bevel: still a gouge, charged at its depth under the bevel.
  - Rest is untouched.
  - An edge nobody declared, or a boss standing above the edge, keeps the model's verdict.
  - `deviate` and `deviate_field` are not touched, so this stays clear of #481's `wall_slack.rs`.
- **Deburr skips steep edges** (generator fix, found while reproducing). The issue said the deburr's deeper gouge columns were link rapids. They were the vertical corner edges. A vertical cone riding a vertical edge, apex `drop` under each point, countersinks the corner down to the window floor. With the default window that is 9.8 mm on the 10 mm brick, a real gouge. The kernel now skips any edge that climbs steeper than the cone's flank, and says so in a path note.
- **Persistence:** the cached path gets an additive `breaks` key (`project/break_dto.rs`). Absent means none, so an old cache is judged against the sharp model until it regenerates (stricter, never looser).
- **Tilted (3+2) frames:** `TiltedFrame::world_path` translates the breaks when the frame is upright and drops them when it is tilted. A posed program is refused by the verdict anyway.
- **Multi-setup programs:** when the program spans setups that hold the part differently, only the final frame's ops' breaks are credited.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/303-op-owns-its-break.md`.

title: fix(post): the Tormach safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
## What changed

The Tormach post's safe retract `G53 G0 Z0` assumed machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. That holds on a Tormach, but on a LinuxCNC machine homed with Z0 at the bottom it rapids down into the part (reported on #435).

- **Machine file:** an optional `safe_retract` on the linear Z part gives the retract Z in MACHINE coordinates, in the file's length unit (scaled like travel). Zero counts as a stated value. A non-number, or the key on any other axis, refuses the file and names the axis. The mirror carries it as `safeRetractZ` (mm). The script sees `machine.safeRetractZ` (or `null`) and `machine.model`, the model name through either door (app mirror or CLI raw file).
- **Shipped machines:** every Tormach `.mch` states `0.0`. So do `vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (`"safeRetractZ": 0.0`).
- **tormach.cps:**
  - A stated safe Z posts `G53 G0 Z<that>`.
  - With no machine, or a model named "Tormach..." that states no safe Z, the output is unchanged (`G53 G0 Z0` + `G30`).
  - Any other machine that states no safe Z gets one counted `message()` that names the machine and the key, and no retract line is written. The in-app gate blocks the write.
  - A non-zero safe Z drops `G30`, because an unset G30 position on LinuxCNC is the machine origin. The header then says `(SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE)`.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/495-safe-retract.md` (alternatives considered, plus notes on the other posts).

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_safe_retract.rs`:
- `the_shipped_tormach_machines_post_byte_identical`: every library Tormach posts byte-identical with and without the key. A null machine and the default VMC also keep `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30`.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers the mirror and the raw door. An inch file scales, there is no G30, and the header comment is written.
- `a_non_tormach_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers the mirror and the raw door, and checks that a Tormach-named file without the key still posts Z0.
- `a_garbled_safe_retract_refuses_the_file`

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all), plus 64 camcraft-app suites touching posts and machines, all green. These include conformance (every golden byte-exact), tormach_post, tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, fanuc_post, inverted_post, program_comments, project_roundtrip, wear_comp and control_comp. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine cut and no Hub sim.
- The UI machine sheet does not show the new key yet.
- The CLI `post` binary was not smoke-run by hand. Its raw-door path is covered by the tests.
- Behaviour change: a document saved before this change with a mounted non-Tormach machine (for example the library "VMC 3-axis") stores that machine without the key. Posting it through the Tormach post is now refused by name until the machine is re-mounted.

Changelog: Tormach post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a non-Tormach machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

title: feat(post): probe positioning moves post as protected stop-on-contact moves
body:
## What changed

The positioning feeds of a probe cycle (the descent from the rapid / safe plane to each touch's start, the bore entry to its centre, the rise back to the safe plane) were plain G01. They now post as protected moves: stop on contact and alarm if the stylus trips on the way.

- **Stream:** `post::dump` marks every non-rapid straight move of a path that carries probing touches, other than the touches and their incremental back-offs, as a new `GUARD x y z F feed` record (`Record::Guard`, `probe_rec::GuardRec`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`). An arc or a feed with no rate in a probe path is refused with a WARN. The safe-plane rapids stay rapids.
- **Engine:** the new `onProbeGuard` hook (properties `X Y Z Feed`, `StartX/Y/Z`). A script without it is refused by name, once per operation. There is no PRELUDE default, because a plain feed would be the silent wrong answer.
- **Fanuc (`fanuc.cps`):** `G31 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then for each moving axis `IF[ABS[#506n-<end>]GT0.001]THEN#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)`. This works because, with no skip signal, the skip position is the block end.
- **Tormach PathPilot (`tormach.cps`):** `G38.3 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then `oN if [#5070 EQ 1]` / `(MSG, PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` / `M2` / `oN endif`, with O-words from 5001.
- **Inverted axes (`invert.rs`):** a GUARD is mirrored like an absolute move.
- **Viewer map (`posting.rs`):** a GUARD counts as one motion record.

Sources (behaviour only): Fanuc's published custom macro B / G31 skip documentation (#5061-#5063, #3000); the LinuxCNC G-code reference (G38.3, #5070, O-code conditionals, MSG); Tormach's PathPilot machine-code reference (G38.2-G38.5 and M2 supported).

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/probe_guard.rs`:
  - `the_positioning_feeds_of_a_probe_path_are_marked_protected`: every mode; no plain feed left; GUARD count per mode; one record per move.
  - `the_guard_record_round_trips_and_refuses_malformed_lines`
  - `fanuc_writes_protected_moves_as_g31_with_a_contact_alarm`: new golden `nc/fanuc/probe_corner.nc`.
  - `tormach_writes_protected_moves_as_g38_3_with_a_trip_test`: new golden `nc/tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`. It pins the guard blocks only, because Tormach's touches are #362 / PR #376.

- Regenerated Fanuc goldens: `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_corner_negative`, `probe_edge_negative_x`. The only change is G01 → G31 + the alarm line.
- `probe_op::the_posted_g31_z_is_the_tip_at_the_expected_contact` now tells touches from guards.
- Gate: these camcraft-app binaries are green, all run on the final head: conformance, fanuc_post, inverted_axis_display, inverted_equivalence, inverted_post, per_op_files, post_not_judged, posting, probe_guard, probe_op, probe_pick, probe_reach, project_roundtrip, scripting, tormach_machines, tormach_post. All camcraft-post tests are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(sim): fixture laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta
body:
Found while gating #339 slice 2 (PR #492): the fixture box laws judged an arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) was missed. This applied to every fixture.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/src/verify/arc_bulge.rs` (`Bulge`, `ARC_PAD` = 1e-3).

**The pad.** For each chord, with ψ = |θ|/2 and θ = sweep/n (the same equal steps `arc_chords` cuts):
- **Across the chord:** r(1 − cos ψ), the sagitta.
- **Along the chord:** r(ψ − sin ψ).

These bound the true point against the chord point at the same sweep fraction for ψ ≤ π/2. Past a half turn, 2r is used for both. Every arc chord adds `ARC_PAD`, because arc centres sit on the 1 µm lattice.

**XY arcs (box laws, `stack_span`):** the band radius grows by `hypot(across, along) + ARC_PAD`. A helix's z between joints is already exact.

**XZ/YZ arcs:**
- The radius grows by `along·|t_h| + across·|n_h| + ARC_PAD`.
- The z window is the arc's true range between joints. Builder-split arcs are Z-monotone, so the strict-dip silence for a lead arc landing tangent on a face is kept.
- An arc that turns past its circle's top or bottom inside a chord gets that piece's window carried to the extremum ± ARC_PAD.

**Posed sweep (`posed_steel`):** an arc move's capsules grow by `Bulge::deviation()`. The interval travel already covered all but about 1e-4 mm; the pad makes the bound hold for any interval length.

**Straight moves get a pad of exactly 0.0,** so every straight verdict is bit-identical.

**Bad arcs fail closed:** a non-finite centre or radius gives a NaN pad, which the predicates read as a hit.

`docs/decisions/491-arc-sagitta.md`

## How tested
New sim `fixture_arc_sagitta` (10 tests). These four fail on main and pass now:
- **The issue's repro:** R30 arc, r3 flute, 3 chords, sagitta 0.00937, box half a sagitta inside the true reach → Flute. The same arc as a rapid → Rapid.
- The holder band is padded too.
- An XZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An unsplit XZ arc dipping past its chords reports.

These also pass, as pins:
- Steel 0.002 mm beyond the true reach stays clean.
- A YZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An XZ arc landing tangent on a face stays silent, while 0.001 deeper hits.
- A posed arc within its sagitta reports.
- Straight moves keep their verdicts.
- The apex sits mid-chord.

**Gates:**
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (all sim suites) is green.
- The full camcraft-app suite, all 170 binaries, is green with **no existing verdict changed**. After the final syntax-only edit, sim in full and the app fixture, rotary, carried, posed-contact, arc-entry and posting suites were re-run, all green.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

**Note:** #476's `mesh_steel` has its own `ARC_PAD` and can read `Bulge::deviation` once both land. #413 is the same family in the field engine and envelope scan, and stays its own issue.

Changelog: Fixture collision laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta, so steel within an arc's bulge is no longer missed (#491)

Fixes #491

The built-in **Lathe** (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`) and **Mill-turn** (`assets/machines/millturn.mch`) stated a machine-frame Z stroke (`-615..0`, `-620..0`). The limit checker (`app::machine::check_document`) reads travel bands in **program coordinates through the work offset** (#457). With Z0 on the face, every move in front of it was out of stroke: clearance, approach, and facing allowance. No turning program posted on either built-in.

Lathe Z is now `-615..615` and Mill-turn Z is `-620..620`. **X stays one-sided** (`0..320`, `0..650`). A lathe X is measured from the spindle centreline, and the centreline is the program's X0, so `0..R` is already a program-frame band. The Mill-turn Y (`-100..100`) was already symmetric. title: feat(app): fixture library - save, insert and delete user fixtures
body:
**Stacked on #482** (#339 slice 4, fixture UX), which is on #476. Slice 6 of #339 per the triage on the issue: a fixture library.

## What changed
**The library file.** One `fixtures.camfixtures` in the user fixtures folder: `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` (an absolute path), otherwise `<data dir>/camcraft/fixtures`, beside the machines folder.
- Versioned envelope: `{format: "camcraft-fixtures", version: 1, units: "mm", fixtures: [{name, note?, datum: {origin, rot}, facets}]}`. Save → load → save is byte-stable.
- **Refused by name, whole file:** bad JSON; wrong format, version or units; a missing name, datum or facets; a duplicate name; an empty mesh; a malformed facet; a rotation that isn't one; over 2M facets; the reserved `Machine/Table` name.
- A missing file reads as an empty library. A corrupt one is reported in the dialog, never shown as empty, and never overwritten.
- The atomic write mirrors #383's machine store. It's a short copy, to be folded into one helper once both land; see the decisions file.

**The datum.**
- An entry's facets are the fixture's own model-frame mesh, and its datum is a frame in that mesh.
- On insert, the model's pose is `P ∘ D⁻¹`, so the datum lands on the pick.
- The default datum is the model origin, so a fixture saved and re-inserted at its old pose stands exactly where it was. The other choice is "Bottom centre".

**Duplicate names:**
- In the library, saving an existing name asks "Replace …?". There is no silent rename.
- In the document, an inserted name that's taken lands as "Vise (2)", "Vise (3)" and so on.

**`InsertFixture`, one undo unit.** It spawns the model with the entry's facets, sets its pose, and tags it to the Fixtures node's setup. It refuses by name a setup that no longer exists, a non-finite or non-rotation pick, or a bad entry. There is no new project key: inserted fixtures are ordinary tagged models.

**Save and delete edit the library file.** They are save actions with confirmation, not undo entries, like machine files (#383).

**UI.** The setup's Fixtures node menu gains **Save fixture to library…** and **Insert from library…**, each a modal dialog.
- **Save:** the setup's fixtures as checkboxes, the datum choice, and a note.
- **Insert:** the entry list, X/Y/Z in display units, and roll/pitch/yaw. Buttons are Insert, **Delete from library…** (with confirmation) and Close.
- Picking the datum in the viewport is a follow-up.

All assets are user-made; no vendor libraries.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-library.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_library` (6 tests):
  - envelope round-trip, and refusals by name;
  - the folder resolver;
  - save, replace and delete file edits;
  - the datum placement maths;
  - insert with undo, redo and the project round-trip.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_library_tests` (4 tests, driven through the real dialog):
  - the menu rows;
  - save, then the replace confirmation;
  - Insert queues one undoable command, and delete happens only after confirmation;
  - a corrupt library is named in the dialog.
- Regressions green: app `fixture_ux` 8, `fixtures` 14, `commands_undo` 32, `fixture_mesh` 3; ui lib 352, ui `tests/fixtures` 7, `tests/models` 4. One #482 test's menu-label list now includes the two new rows.

- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

A hands-on check. The test kit is prepared and sandboxed with `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES`.

This is the follow-up to #402 / PR #414. Two more places drew XY arcs (G2/G3 in G17) as chords inside the arc: the **field engine** (`field_cut::chords`) and the **envelope scan** that runs while toolpaths are generated (`stock_sim/scan.rs`). Both now read the true circle.

**Field engine:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_arc.rs`, 284 lines, with a provenance header.
- An upright mill tool's XY arc is now cut as `Sweep::Arc` pieces.
- Pieces follow the old chord budget, capped at a quarter turn. So the lattice windows and the `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` limit refuse exactly what they refused before. Each window grows by its piece's sagitta.
- **Level piece:** solved exactly in closed form. The nearest tool pose is at the point's own bearing, clamped to the piece. It uses the column engine's tie rules (`flat_tie`, `bull_tie`), and `field_ray` gets the exact floor plane from it.
- **Helical piece:** searched with `dexel_arc::piece_min`, #414's search (samples, then a golden section). Every result is a real distance evaluation plus the usual 1e-12 margin, so the field never shows material removed that the tool did not cut. Its `residual` is a proven bound: half a sample step of tool travel.
- Tilted tools, lathe tools and XZ/YZ arcs keep their chords.

**Envelope scan:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_arc.rs`, 146 lines.
- Each arc piece keeps the chord `arc_chords` drew. That chord is now only used for indexing (bins, boxes, ring ids, the ridge law's pass counting), so all of that is unchanged.
- Every distance the verdict uses is now measured to the arc:
  - point distances for rest, flank and hidden rest (exact for level arcs);
  - facet distances for gouge, searched only when the chord is within the piece's bulge of the ball.
- The gouge bin walk, the ridge boxes and the `SegGrid` ring prune each grow by the bulge (`sag + |dz|`), so no contact the chords caught can be missed.

**Tests tightened:** `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike` now holds the helix arc to the same 1e-5 engine parity as straight moves, and the `arc_parity` relaxation is removed.

The decisions and the dropped alternatives (straddling chords, finer chords, one whole-arc sweep) are in `docs/decisions/413-arc-chords-field.md`.

## Pinning tests
- **New `sim/tests/field_arc_sweep.rs`** (5 tests; 4 fail on the old code):
  - `the_field_cuts_every_tool_on_the_true_arc_like_the_column`: flat, ball, cone and bull tools on level and helical arcs, CW and CCW, including a sweep past half a turn and one with a radius smaller than the tool. The field's top matches the column engine's to 1e-5.
  - `the_bull_helix_rim_is_cut_on_the_field_too`: the #414 helix (bull r 2, corner 0.75). Rim columns are cut more than 2 mm deep, matching the column engine to 1e-5.
  - `a_clean_convex_corner_arc_reads_no_gouge_on_the_field`: a column 0.06 mm inside a riser corner. The old chords cut it 10 mm deep, top 28 → 15. Now it is untouched and reads no gouge.
  - `a_convex_corner_arc_cut_too_tight_is_still_a_gouge_on_the_field`: a planted twin that is still convicted at 10 mm.
  - `a_concave_fillet_wall_loses_exactly_the_columns_the_true_arc_reaches`: a fillet over-cut by 0.06 mm. Exactly the wall columns the true arc reaches are cut.
- **New `sim/tests/scan_arc.rs`** (2 tests; both fail on the old code):
  - `a_ball_rolled_round_an_outside_corner_reads_no_gouge`: the old code read 0.0092 mm of phantom gouge.
  - `a_wall_the_true_arc_dips_into_reads_the_dip`: the old code read 0, the true value is 0.0045 mm.
- `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike`: back to 1e-5 parity on the arc.

## Readings
- **Debug:** all `camcraft-sim` suites pass. All `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion` suites pass, including the slow finish3d, pivot5d, flow and center_cut_multiaxis: 2028 passed, 0 failed.
- **Release heavy lanes** (`--ignored`, sim + motion + app): 64 passed, 0 failed.
- **No golden changed.**
- **clippy:** `-p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The GPU and headless UI tests: `camcraft-ui` was not touched, and its GPU headless tests are known to fail on this machine.
- A hand check of the displayed stock in the GUI.
- The rotary field (`field_rotary`), which has its own chord law and is untouched.
- **Cost:** a helical piece costs about the same as the old golden-section chord (8 samples plus a 32-round golden section, against 32 rounds). A level piece costs one evaluation. Cost was not benchmarked beyond the suite times, which did not move noticeably.

title: fix(sim): judge a gouge with tol of lateral slack at a wall
body:
## What changed

The program sim's gouge verdict judged each column by height alone, at its centre. A height verdict's normal-distance tolerance is `tol * cos(slope)`, which is zero at a vertical wall. So a column whose centre sits a few microns inside a wall, reached by a tool that finishes that wall within tolerance, was charged the wall's whole height, and the post gate refused a correct program.

- New `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_slack.rs`: a gouge candidate (a column more than `tol` below the part's top at its centre) is re-judged against the lowest part top within `tol` of its centre. That is the centre plus an eight-direction ring at radius `tol`, and air counts as lowest. If the column is within `tol` of that lowest top, it is clean. Otherwise it is a gouge, charged at the centre's own depth as before.
- Both engines use it: the column engine (`deviate`) and the field arm (`deviate_field`), keeping the stage-C parity law.
- Rest is unchanged: it is still judged against the centre's own top.
- The extra cost is paid only when gouge candidates exist. A clean program costs nothing extra.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/299-wall-column-gouge.md`. It covers why the slack is `tol` and not the issue's `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, cell)`, and the other options that were dropped.

## Readings (current main 5fd2b93)

- The issue's exact 2D Contour repro (model stock, 10 mm deep) **no longer reproduces on main**: the gate is clean before and after this change. It is kept as a regression test.
- 3D Finish, `BN-0600`, kind defaults, model stock (the issue's MCP job): before, `gouge: ... 1 cell(s), worst 10.21 mm at (16.69, -24.91, z 9.79)`. Probing that column, its centre is 1-3 um inside the D's wall, with air beyond. After: no gouge. The post is still blocked, by the generator's own `ShankHit` warnings, which is a separate matter.
- 3D Finish in the issue's 70 x 70 x 27 box at z -7: before, 37 cells, worst 22.01 mm at (-26.56, 13.94). After: 0 gouge cells.

## Tests

- `crates/sim/tests/wall_slack.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_column_a_few_microns_inside_a_finished_wall_is_not_a_gouge`: both engines, with a floor beside the wall and with air beside it. This test fails on main.
  - `the_old_law_charged_that_column_the_whole_wall`
  - `a_real_gouge_into_a_wall_still_convicts_at_its_full_depth`: covers 50 um, 12 um and 1 mm intrusions, in both engines, and checks the full 15 mm depth and location.
  - `a_floor_gouge_away_from_walls_is_unchanged`
  - `rest_beside_a_wall_keeps_the_centres_own_top`
- `crates/app/tests/wall_column_gouge.rs` (new, 3 tests):
  - `a_3d_finish_on_the_users_part_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `a_3d_finish_in_the_users_box_stock_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `the_issues_contour_on_model_stock_reads_no_gouge`
- Gate results:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: all green.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app` (all 169 binaries, debug): all green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- Release `--ignored` lanes:
  - sim `hidden_rest_banded`, app `operations` and `rotary_field_parity`: green.
  - app `stock_engine_agreement` has 2 tests (`both_engines_judge_every_golden_program_alike`, `the_feed_sampler_reads_every_golden_program_alike`) that **fail identically on upstream/main** (6467 FINDING lines, for example `contour_disc_hole.cl` column (46.25, -4.25) and `finish3d_scallop_plateau.cl+bull` engagement). This is pre-existing and not caused by this PR. Diffing the findings between main and this branch shows 5 lines changed: field-arm micro-readings on `finish3d_project_dome.cl` (field dev -0.011 to -0.016 on the slope) now read clean instead of gouge. That is the expected slope allowance (at most `tol * tan(slope)`). No column-engine verdict changed, and no golden changed.

## Not exercised

- GUI Deviate view, by eye.
- A real cut.
- `kernel::measure` / `measure_field` (the per-op reports, not the post gate) keep the centre-only law.
- #303 (chamfer/deburr false gouge) is **not** fixed by this. Its bevel is a sloped cut 0.74-3.8 mm deep, far past a 10 um slack, and needs the op-owns-its-break law the issue describes.

Changelog: The post gate no longer refuses a correct program for a gouge at a wall: a sim column within the 0.01 mm tolerance of a vertical wall is judged against the floor beside it, while a cut past that still refuses (#299)

Fixes #299

Follow-up to #287 (first slice: #382, the read-only Machines pane, merged).

## What changed
**Machines pane: create, edit and save `.mch` machine files.**
- **New:** **New blank** (mill, lathe or mill-turn, starting from the keys that kind requires), **New from template** (copies the selected machine), and **Edit machine**.
- **Property grid** with nine collapsible groups: General, Axes and travels, Rotaries and limits, Spindle range, Feeds, Tool changer and stations, Coolant codes, Live-tool codes, Units. Each field's tooltip names its key.
- **Validation.** `machine::validate` (from #382) runs live.
  - Each refusal is shown in red under its field. Refusals that belong to no field (for example a missing required axis) are listed above the grid.
  - **Save and Save As are disabled while any refusal stands**, so a refused file is never written.
- **Save / Save As.**
  - Save asks "Write <path>?" before writing.
  - Save As asks for a name in the user folder, and asks again before replacing an existing file.
  - Closing with unsaved edits asks before discarding them.
  - After a save the list is re-read and the new file is selected.
- **Shipped machines are read-only.** A built-in machine, or a file under `assets/machines`, opens read-only, and Save on it opens Save As.
- **Atomic write:** a temp file in the same folder, synced, then renamed.
- **Unknown keys are kept.** Edits are made on the file's raw JSON, so keys the editor doesn't know survive a save.
- **User folder:** `CAMCRAFT_MACHINES` (absolute paths only), otherwise `<platform data dir>/camcraft/machines`. Resolved in the app layer (`machine::store`), and the pane's list includes it.
- **Not an undoable project edit.** Saving a machine *file* queues no command and adds nothing to the undo history, per the issue. Assigning a machine to a setup is #384.
- **Code:** new app modules `machine/{store,fields,draft}.rs`; new UI `machine_file_editor.rs`. The existing Setup-pane `machine_editor.rs` is unchanged.

body:

The built-in **VMC 3-axis** (`assets/machines/vmc.mch`) and **Tilt-head 5-axis** (`assets/machines/tilthead.mch`) stated machine-frame strokes (Z `-500..0`, X `±300`, Y `±250`), but the limit checker (`app::machine::check_document`) reads travel bands in **program coordinates through the work offset**. Fix: restate both files the way the Tormach files already are (b189c960): a slide of stroke L is `-L..L`, the full stroke either way, because the file cannot know where the work offset sits along the slide. Now Z `-500..500`, X `-600..600`, Y `-500..500`. No checker code changed. The rule is written down in the `app::machine` module doc and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`. Test-fixture comments in `tilt.rs`, `rotary_verify.rs` and `post_not_judged.rs` that cited the old `-500..0` band were updated (comments only). The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/457-vmc-z-stroke.md`.

- New `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs`:
  - `a_plate_contour_on_the_built_in_vmc_passes_the_stroke_and_posts`: the issue's repro (2D Contour on a 1 mm plate, clearance Z 26, built-in VMC as the document machine). `check_document` is clean, `verification_report` has no problems, and `post_setup` posts.   - `a_clearance_past_the_vmc_column_still_refuses_by_name`: clearance Z 520 is refused with `2D Contour1: move N reaches 520.000 in Z, the stroke is -500.000..500.000`, and the post is refused.

title: feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh
body:
**Replaces #430**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so it can no longer be updated. This branch carries the merges with main through #461: the mesh law reads #381's `HolderStack` (`steel_stack(geom, holder, spindle)`, with `mesh_refined` wrapping the `*_held` laws), and #395's turning holder judge is kept. The recipe in the old 'merge note for #381' below is now done.

Slice 1 of #339 (triage and split are on the issue). Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh, so a path down a vise's gap posts clean.

## What changed
**The box laws still run first, and the mesh can only clear a hit.** When a fixture's world box flags an upright move (laws c2 and d2), the fixture's closed mesh gets the final say, and it can only clear that hit, never add one. That keeps the box laws' deliberate silences, such as a retract off the mounting face. Where nothing is cleared, output is identical to before, labels included.

**Test shape.** Each tool band (flute, shank, holder, and the spindle housing when stated) is an upright cylinder swept along the move, an exact convex shape. Arcs are split into chords, each padded by how far the true arc can stray from it, plus 1 µm.

**Why it can't miss a real hit:**
- A band counts as clear only when a GJK distance test proves a gap of more than `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (plus the arc pad) to every nearby triangle. If the search fails or runs out, the answer is a hit.
- A band far from every triangle could still be buried inside the solid, so a point of it is tested by ray parity. Six fixed off-axis rays are tried; any that graze an edge, vertex or face are discarded, and if all are ambiguous the point counts as inside.
- Only closed meshes judge (each edge used once in each direction).
- A bounding-volume tree over the triangles is pruned with the same proof at every node.

**What keeps the box verdict:**
- Meshes that are open, non-finite, fully collapsed or over 4M facets: a named `MeshError`, logged.
- Tilted moves, moves with a non-zero C angle, and XZ/YZ arcs.
- Lathe tool kinds and non-mill machines.
- A box shared by two fixtures.

**Performance (release):**
- A 203k-facet closed mesh: validate and build the tree in 0.05 s.
- Worst case, 2000 passes grazing it 0.05 mm off (every one inside its box): 0.74 s total (0.37 ms/move), all correctly cleared.

**Code:**
- New: `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/` (mod, gjk, bvh, ray), `crates/sim/src/verify/mesh_steel.rs`.
- Hooks: `fixture::meshes_for`, plus small edits in `operation/{job,generate}.rs` and `posting.rs` (meshes cached once per setup).
- `docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md`

**Merge note for #381:** this edits next to #381's `HolderStack` changes in `posting.rs` `fixture_problems` and `generate.rs` `workholding_warnings`. Whichever lands second resolves by keeping `mesh_refined(path, &wh, &steel, rapids, |w| <law>)` with the closures calling #381's `_held` variants, and by building `steel_stack` from the `HolderStack` bands. The decisions file has the recipe.

## How tested
- `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (8 tests, plus one in the heavy lane):
  - a vise-gap pass, plunge and arc are cleared;
  - a jaw-corner clip still hits, while the same line 4.95 mm off is cleared;
  - a jaw-face clip, a holder over a jaw, a rapid into a jaw top, and a tool buried in steel all still hit;
  - open, NaN, empty and collapsed meshes refuse by name and keep the box verdict;
  - a tilted move and a fixture-less table box keep the box verdict;
  - timings (heavy lane: the 200k-facet case).
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (3 tests), end to end through `posting::verification_gate` and regeneration:
  - vise jaws 3 mm off the pass: clean;
  - the same vise as an open sheet: box verdict;
  - jaws 1 mm into the pass: the post is blocked and generation warns.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`: sim suites green; app suites green except `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…`, which is red on plain main (#415). Every existing fixture suite is unchanged.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised / follow-ups
- **Two P0 gaps in the existing box laws** were found by this survey and filed separately: #424 (upright rapids check only the flute) and #425 (ramps judged at their lowest z). This slice does not fix them, since the mesh only clears hits. The triage's slice 2 makes the mesh law able to add hits too.
- The remaining #339 slices: tilted and rotary moves against the mesh, fixture UX, routing around fixtures, and a fixture library.
- No GUI change, and no change to posted G-code. More programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
> Replaces #428, moved to the new fork (the old one left NeoTech's network; a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in; the one conflict was the module list in `mcp/mod.rs`, where both sides are kept. `mcp` 9/9, `mcp_live` 6/6 and `mcp_pick` 2/2 pass, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (refreshed binaries `camcraft-ui-428` and `camcraft-cli-428`).

## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. Hand run: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7333` driven through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` (set_stock, add_tool, add_operation all `isError:false`; `get_job` over nc showed the op in the app's world).

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`: `a_live_call_lands_on_the_callers_history_and_its_undo_reverts_it`, `each_agent_step_is_one_undo_step_on_the_shared_history`, `the_live_session_refuses_open_project_and_reads_bad_lines_as_errors`, `the_port_flag_is_opt_in_and_checked`, `a_loopback_client_drives_the_owners_document_and_survives_bad_input` (real loopback TCP), `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::mcp_live`: `an_agents_operation_shows_in_the_browser_and_ctrl_z_removes_it`, `the_status_strip_says_the_server_is_listening`.

## Not exercised
Ctrl+Z pressed by hand in the real window (harness only) - **draft until the GUI check**; Windows/Linux runs (std::net only); a real MCP client app beyond the bridge/nc; the bind-failure path (port in use). Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/183-mcp-live-gui.md`.

Changelog: The GUI can serve MCP live on a loopback port (`--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`), so an agent's steps land in the open document and Ctrl+Z undoes them; `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` bridges stdio clients

Fixes #183

**Tool editor: a "Tool body" column.**
- **Import body…** (STEP/STL/OBJ through the app's importer) and **Clear body**.
- Placement controls: an axis combo (±X/±Y/±Z of the model, or a picked direction), **Tip offset**, and **Pick tip** / **Pick axis** toggles.
- A small 3D preview: egui-painted, drag to orbit, no GPU.
- A live placement note ("placed: foot … to top …" or the reason it won't place), and **Apply body**.
- The 2D profile preview draws the placed body's revolved envelope in amber over the cylinders.
- A tool not yet in the document shows "Add the tool first…".

**Picking.** A click casts a ray through `tool_body_view::pick`.
- **Pick tip** snaps to the nearest corner of the hit facet and sets the offset so that corner is the tip.
- **Pick axis** takes the clicked facet's outward normal.
- Picks only fill the fields; they never queue a command.

**Commands.**
- **Apply body** queues one `SetToolBody`, a single undo step. **Clear body** is the same command with `None`.
- Refusals show in the editor by name ("tool body not set: …", "tool body not imported: …") and the draft is kept.
- The draft reloads only when the world's body changes (Apply / Undo / Redo / Open), so an unapplied import survives other edits.

**Simulation.** While the transport runs, the running tool's body is posed at the playhead (read from the cached timeline) and drawn as a shaded, depth-tested part. A tool without a body draws exactly as before.

**App-layer helpers**, so ui stays thin: `crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs` holds `load`, `preview` (the same place-and-envelope step as the command, uncommitted), `pick`, `tip_offset_at`, `posed` and `body_for_operation`.

`docs/decisions/371-tool-body-ui.md` records why picking lives in the editor's own preview rather than the main viewport. Among other reasons, a pick mode there would compete with the face/edge/vertex picks.

title: feat(app): Pause, optional stop and go-home entries in the operation list
body:
**Replaces #427**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #427 can no longer be updated. This branch also carries the merge with main at #461.

## What changed
**A new program-entry kind: Pause (M0), Optional stop (M1) and Go home.**
- Entries sit in the operation list alongside operations, using the same `OperationMeta.order`.
- The new component `schema::ProgramEntry { action, setup, suppressed }` is not an `Operation`. So `setup::operation_order`, and every walk built on it, skips entries without per-walk carve-outs: the post tool gate and freshness, `rest::ahead_of`, the program sim, the setup sheet, the tool list, verify and `RegenerateAll`.
- An entry has no generated status, so it never holds the post as "not generated".

**Posting.** Each entry folds into the posted op before it, as that op's `PARAM AfterOperation` word (one hook in `posting::op_streams`, logic in `program_entry::posted_afters`).
- A Pause after Face1 posts byte-identically to setting Face1's after-action to Program stop. This is pinned for all three actions on Fanuc and Haas.
- Equal asks in one gap merge, and a program stop absorbs an optional stop.
- An entry after a suppressed op attaches to the last op that posts.
- Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes" mute entries just as they mute op actions.
- **Refused by name:**
  - an entry before every posted op;
  - a Pause and a Home in the same gap (the stream holds one after-word per gap);
  - entries on the Tormach post, which doesn't read `AfterOperation`, the same as the per-op action there today.

**Commands, all undoable.**
- New: `AddProgramEntry` (after a named row, or at the end of the active setup), `EditProgramEntry::with_action` and `::with_suppressed`.
- Reused: `ReorderOperation` (drag) and `DeleteEntity` (Del or the menu).
- `ReorderOperation`, `CreateOperation`'s append and `DeleteSetup`'s refusal now count over `program_entry::sequence`, which equals `operation_order` on documents without entries.

**UI.**
- Every operation-list menu gains "Add pause (M0) after", "Add go home after" and "Add optional stop (M1) after".
- An entry row uses the Post glyph, with its action and SUPPRESSED in the suffix. Its menu offers change action, suppress, delete and add after.
- Entries drag like op rows.

**Project file: no version rung.**
- An entry saves as `"kind": "entry"` plus an `entry` payload.
- A document without entries writes neither key, so its bytes are unchanged.
- An older reader refuses a file with entries (serde: unknown variant `entry`) rather than dropping the stops.

**Posted G-code:** only documents with entries change. No `.cps` was touched, and every existing golden is unchanged.

`docs/decisions/155-pause-home-entries.md`

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.

title: feat(post): probing on an inverted X/Y axis for the Fanuc post
body:
Part of #372. Lifts the #374 refusal of probing on an inverted X/Y, for Fanuc. Haas follows when its probing hooks land (PR #360), hence `Refs #392`.

## What changed
- **Translation.** `post::invert` mirrors the probing records on an inverted X/Y, the same way it mirrors a move. It negates the TOUCH target and expected trip, the RETREAT back-off delta and its end point, and each FOUND axis's expected value.
- **New manifest flag `probeAxisInversion = true`.** The translation runs only for a post script that declares it, and only `fanuc.cps` does. Haas declares `axisInversion` but not this flag, so it refuses probing by name. Posts without `axisInversion` already refuse any inverted machine.

**Why negating is right.** The controller position is `M = G54 + P`, and the tip stands at `S·M`, where S = −1 on the inverted axis.
- The posted `P = S(W − origin)` lands correctly only if G54 holds `S·D`.
- A part off by d trips at `S(W_trip + d − origin)`. The translated expected value is `S(W_trip − origin)`, so the deviation is `S·d`.
- `G10 L2 X[#5221+dev]` then gives `S(D + d)`: the real part's datum in controller coordinates.
- Back-offs are increments, so they flip with the axis. `ABS[dev]` and the choice of travel axis are sign-free.
- In full: `docs/decisions/392-probe-inverted-axis.md`.

## How tested
New `inverted_probe` (8 tests). The posted Fanuc programs run on a **test-only macro-B controller** (`crates/app/tests/macro_b/`): G31 trips where the stylus first meets a simulated part, every G0/G1 is collision-checked, and unmodelled words are errors.
- **Physical offset:** face −Z, face −X, edge −Y, corners +X+Y and −X−Y, bore and boss, each on standard, inverted-X, inverted-Y and inverted-XY machines, with the part shifted (0.37, −0.21, −0.13) mm.
  - G55 always ends at the physical datum, within 0.002.
  - G54 is untouched, and unmeasured axes aren't written.
  - The standard machine gives the same answer, which checks the interpreter.
- **Edge cases:** a part exactly on the model returns the datum unchanged. No contact raises `#3000=2`, and out of tolerance raises `#3000=1`.
- **Converse checks:** the untranslated program misses on an inverted machine. Undoing any one translated word breaks it: a stylus crash, a tolerance alarm, or probing past overtravel.
- **Both sign forms:** the reader accepts the old `#100--2.5` and the folded `#100+2.5` from #386, which is now on main. Re-run after merging main: 8/8.
- **Existing suites:** `inverted_post`, `inverted_equivalence`, `axis_direction`, `probe_op`, `probe_reach`, `fanuc_post`, `conformance` and the camcraft-post suites pass. **No golden changed.** `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except #415, which is red on main.

No run on a real control with an inverted axis. The macro interpreter proves the arithmetic and motion of the posted words.

title: fix(ui): macOS Cmd+Q asks about unsaved changes
body:
> Replaces #334, which GitHub closed when its review fix was pushed after the fork left NeoTech's network. It includes that fix: `os_quit::request()` is `#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", test))]`, so it is not dead code on Windows or Linux under clippy. The hands-on Cmd+Q check on macOS passed (see #334).

## What changed

On macOS, Cmd+Q, the app menu's Quit, the Dock's Quit and a logout all send `terminate:` to NSApplication. winit 0.30.13's app delegate has no `applicationShouldTerminate:`, so AppKit ended the process at once. `CloseRequested` never arrived, and the unsaved-changes prompt (#107) was skipped. The menu also takes Cmd+Q before egui sees it, so the egui Cmd/Ctrl+Q shortcut never fired on macOS either.

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/os_quit.rs`. On macOS, `install()` adds `applicationShouldTerminate:` to winit's delegate class through `class_addMethod`. The method answers `NSTerminateCancel` and only sets an atomic flag, so nothing can unwind across the FFI boundary. `class_addMethod` never replaces a method: if a future winit adds its own handler, the hook logs that and stays out. A missing AppKit, app or delegate is logged, never a panic. On other platforms `install()` does nothing.
- `route_pending(state)` turns the flag into `actions::quit`, the same guarded Quit the window X sends. The shell calls it in `about_to_wait`, and un-minimises and focuses the window so the prompt is seen. A clean document quits through `el.exit()`, which does not go back through `terminate:`.
- Dependency: `objc2 0.5`, the same binding and version winit already pulls in. It is macOS-only (`[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]`), and no new crate enters `Cargo.lock`.

Decisions and the alternatives dropped are recorded in `docs/decisions/144-macos-cmd-q.md`: retargeting the menu item, replacing winit's default menu, and routing to `performClose:`.

Side effect: cancelling the terminate also cancels a logout or shutdown while CamCraft is open, and macOS says CamCraft stopped it. That is the usual document-app behaviour. Letting the logout continue after the user answers was left out.

## Readings

- winit 0.30.13: `platform_impl/macos/menu.rs` wires Quit to `terminate:`, and `app_state.rs` implements only `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` and `applicationWillTerminate:`.
- Live run on a Mac: a debug build with a clean document, sent `terminate:` via `NSRunningApplication.terminate`. The request went through the hook, and the app then exited with code 0.

## Pinning test

- `egui_app::tests::unsaved::os_quit_request_over_unsaved_changes_prompts_once`: an OS quit request over unsaved work is routed once, does not exit, and shows "Unsaved changes"; Don't Save then quits.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` ran as batch (Cargo files touched). Green apart from the known swarf_pose_continuity and the GPU-adapter headless tests (headless_run_succeeds, egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero, headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero: no graphics adapter in this environment). clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Manual check (needs a Mac)

1. `cargo run -p camcraft-ui`, then make the document dirty (the title gets `*`).
2. Press Cmd+Q. The prompt should appear. Click Cancel: the app stays open.
3. Choose app menu > Quit. The prompt should appear. Click Don't Save: the app quits.
4. Make it dirty again and minimise. Right-click the Dock icon > Quit. The window should come back with the prompt.
5. With a clean document, Cmd+Q quits at once.
